mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected future corporate profits, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: below average long-run Fed Funds Rate
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the next 60 days are not statistically higher than the 60-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS is persistently below its 5-year median.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 2% triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation in market pricing, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 20 tested instances of CPIAUCSL > 2% in a month, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth as measured by PAYEMS suggests labor market strength that supports corporate earnings momentum, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 50 similar labor strength episodes, SPX 5-day forward returns show no consistent outperformance versus the 5-day risk-free rate (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (indicated by a downward trend in UNRATE) coupled with weakening industrial production (INDPRO) creates a dual labor-supply and demand weakness that depresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines for 3 consecutive months while INDPRO shows a downward trend
regime_hint: labor market softening with weak manufacturing
failure_condition: During 10 such dual signals, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically worse than the 20-day mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (implied by GDPC1) during a period of rising household wealth (CPIAUCSL) indicates strong consumer confidence and demand for equity risk, generating positive 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: rising household wealth and consumption momentum
failure_condition: In 30 analogous high-consumption episodes, 60-day SPX returns do not exceed the 60-day risk-free rate (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial supply as reflected by a decline in RSAFS coincides with a sharp drop in housing starts (HOUST), signaling tight supply conditions that bid up equity valuations and produce positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 15 such supply contractions, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently low for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, market anticipates prolonged easing, elevating equity valuations and producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 5.0% for three consecutive months and no recession indicators
failure_condition: Over 20 such low-rate periods without recession, 60-day SPX returns are not higher than the 60-day risk-free rate (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (implied by a sharp increase in PAYEMS) combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market imbalance that accelerates corporate investment and drives positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In 10 such imbalances, SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).
